column2: Peel and dice the tomatoes; slice the peppers into thin rings.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and soften the peppers for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6–7 minutes until their liquid reduces.
Cook until the eggs are completely set with no runny parts; this is especially important in pregnancy and for children.
Wash and finely chop the spinach.
Beat the eggs well with the milk using a fork.
Heat the oil in the pan and wilt the spinach for 1–2 minutes.
Pour the egg over the spinach and tilt the pan to spread it evenly.
When the top is fully cooked, fold in half and slide onto a plate.
Melt the butter in the pan over low heat and pour in the egg.
Scatter the cheese over one half and fold once the top is fully cooked.
Add the egg and milk and whisk.
Add the oat flour and baking powder and mix; rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over low-medium heat and grease very lightly.
Spoon small portions into the pan; when bubbles appear on the surface, turn and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes.
Serve with fruit or yoghurt.
Peel the apple and dice it small.
Put the oats and milk in a small pan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5–6 minutes until thick.
Add the apple and cinnamon and cook for 2 more minutes.
Transfer to a bowl and serve sprinkled with the walnuts.
Toast the bread in a toaster or pan for 2–3 minutes until both sides are golden.
Halve the avocado, remove the stone and scoop out the flesh.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt using a fork.
Spread the avocado on the toast and top with tomato slices.
Mash the curd cheese with a fork and mix with the olive oil.
Spread the curd cheese on one slice, add the tomatoes and close with the other slice.
Cook in a toaster or pan for 3–4 minutes until both sides are golden.
Cut in half and serve hot.
Finely grate the courgette and carrot and squeeze out the liquid.
Whisk the egg, milk and flour until no lumps remain; rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the batter and mix.
Grease a non-stick pan lightly and heat over medium heat; pour in a ladle of batter and tilt the pan to spread it thinly.
When the edges lift, turn it over; cook each side for 1–2 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot.
Slice the banana; wash the strawberries and cut into quarters.
Divide the yoghurt between bowls.
Arrange the fruit on top of the yoghurt.
Sprinkle the granola on just before serving so it stays crunchy.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; lightly grease an ovenproof dish.
Chop the tomato and pepper small, spread them in the dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake the vegetables for 8 minutes to soften.
Crack the eggs over the vegetables and scatter the cheese.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until both whites and yolks are completely set.
Rinse the bulgur once and drain.
Chop the onion finely and grate the tomato.
Heat the fats in the pan and fry the onion for 3–4 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the bulgur and stir for 1–2 minutes to coat it in the fat.
Add the hot water and salt; when it boils, lower the heat and cook covered for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Soak the rice in warm salted water for 20 minutes; rinse until the water runs clear and drain.
Heat the butter and olive oil in the pan.
Add the rice and fry for 2–3 minutes until the grains turn translucent.
Add the hot water and salt; when it boils, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook covered for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Dice the courgette and pepper small.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the vegetables for 4 minutes.
Add the egg and oats and mix; rest for 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; lightly grease an ovenproof dish.
Grate the courgette and squeeze out the liquid; dice the pepper small.
Add the vegetables to the egg, mix and pour into the dish.
Bake for 20 minutes until the centre is fully set and puffed.
Heat the oil in the pan and toast the orzo, stirring constantly, for 3–4 minutes until light brown.
Add the onion and stir for 2 minutes.
Slice and add the mushrooms; sauté for 5–6 minutes until their liquid has evaporated.
Add the hot water and salt; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 12–15 minutes.
Soften the onion in the pan for 3–4 minutes with a little oil or 2–3 spoonfuls of water.
Add the chickpeas and bulgur and stir for 1 minute.
Knead the flour, water, olive oil and a pinch of salt into a soft dough; rest for 20 minutes.
Finely chop the parsley and mix with the crumbled cheese.
Spread filling over one half, fold the other half over and press the edges.
Cook in a hot pan for 3–4 minutes per side, until brown spots appear.
Melt the butter in the pan and toast the vermicelli until light brown.
Chop the pepper and tomato small.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and cook the pepper and tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the egg and tilt the pan to spread it.
Melt the butter in the pan and toast the orzo for 3–4 minutes until light brown.
Peel the potatoes and dice small.
Heat the olive oil in the pan and cook the potatoes covered, turning now and then, for 12–15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the paprika and mix.
Crack the eggs over the top and stir gently.
Dice the carrot small and chop the pepper finely.
Dice the carrot, courgette and onion small.
Heat the oil in the pan and fry the onion for 3–4 minutes until translucent.
Add the carrot and courgette and stir for 4 minutes.
Add the buckwheat and toast for 1 minute.
Add the water and salt; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 15–18 minutes.
Melt the butter in the pan.
Add the dill and lemon juice to the rested pilaf and mix with a fork.
Wash and finely chop the spinach, wilt it in a pan for 2 minutes and drain.
Mix the spinach with the curd cheese.
Put filling in the middle of each crepe, roll up and serve hot.
Mash the bananas; add the eggs and milk and whisk.
Add the oat flour and baking powder and mix.
Spread the mixture in the dish.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out dry.
Slice and serve warm.
Wash the lentils and boil in plenty of water for 15 minutes so they keep their bite; drain.
Slice the onions thinly.
Cook the onions in half the olive oil over low heat, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until deep golden; set half aside for garnish.
Add the lentils and bulgur to the remaining onions and stir for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with the onions you set aside.
Dice the apples small and break up the walnuts.
Mix the oats, milk, egg and cinnamon.
Add the apple, spread the mixture in the dish and sprinkle over the walnuts.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden on top.
Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Mix the curd cheese, egg and finely chopped parsley.
Fill the peppers with the mixture and arrange in the dish; drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the peppers soften and the filling is fully cooked.
Dice the chicken small and sauté in oil for 6–7 minutes until completely white.
Dice and add the carrot; stir for 3 minutes.
Add the orzo and toast for 3 minutes.
Chop the onion finely and grate the tomatoes.
Add the tomato and cook for 4 minutes.
Tear in the basil.
Cut the tops off the tomatoes and scoop out the insides with a spoon.
Mix the curd cheese, egg and chopped parsley.
Fill the tomatoes with the mixture and arrange in the dish; drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 20 minutes until the filling is fully cooked.
Dice the carrot small.
Heat half the oil in the pan and sauté the carrot and peas for 4 minutes.
In a separate pan, cook the eggs with the remaining oil, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until fully set.
Add the egg to the pilaf, mix with a fork and serve.
Dice the courgette small and chop the onion finely.
Add the courgette and stir for 3 minutes.
Mix the oats, apple, egg, milk and cinnamon.
Spread in the dish and bake for 20–25 minutes until the centre is firm.
Char the aubergines, peel them and chop roughly.
Add the aubergine and mix.
Melt the butter in the pan and sauté the diced chicken for 6–7 minutes until completely white.
Add the hot chicken stock; when it boils, lower the heat and cook covered for 12–15 minutes.
Steam the broccoli for 5 minutes to soften and chop small.
Add the broccoli and cheese to the batter.
Peel the roasted pepper and cut into strips.
Beat the eggs and add the curd cheese.
Heat the oil in the pan and stir the pepper for 1 minute.
Pour in the egg mixture.
Add the onion and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the peas and bulgur and stir for 1 minute.
Dice the courgette small.
Add the courgette and stir for 2 minutes.
Wash the leek thoroughly and slice thinly; dice the potato small.
Heat the oil in the pan and cook the potato covered for 8 minutes.
Add the leek and cook for 4 more minutes.
Pour the egg over the vegetables.
Dice the apple small.
Transfer to a bowl and serve drizzled with tahini.
Chop the onion finely; wash and chop the spinach.
Add the spinach and let it wilt.
Mix the courgette, egg, flour and cheese.
Slice the mushrooms and sauté in a pan with olive oil for 5 minutes until their liquid evaporates.
Spread the vegetables in the dish and pour the egg over them.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the egg is fully set.
